example-embed.name: Example Embed
example-embed.description: Minimal embed preset: 3D only, source panels hidden, Image Georeferencer hidden, hillshade + hypsometric tint on by default.

mapterhorn-globe.name: Mapterhorn Globe
mapterhorn-globe.description: Minimal globe view zoomed out to the whole world, Mapterhorn as the only terrain source, source pickers and Image Georeferencer hidden, GMT Globe hypsometric ramp.

dura.name: Dura Frescoes Viewer
dura.description: Dura Europos Synagogue COG terrain + basemap (W-0.5mm), fixed 2D view over the site, hillshade on (hypsometric tint off), raster basemap at 20% opacity, Relief Visualization and Terrain Analysis available but off, contours/mound-detector/split-screen/elevation-picker off and hidden, 2D/3D view modes only (no globe), sidebar closed by default, source pickers hidden, Visualization Modes and Hillshade Options sections open, map controls disabled, Bookmarks/Source-Info/Sun-Shadow-Calculator/Image-Georeferencer sections and the General Settings Project + Open-in controls hidden, light pinned to Free mode (no Free/Datetime selector), Shadows sub-mode off and hidden.

moon-south-pole.name: Moon - LOLA south pole 5 m (beta)
moon-south-pole.description: Moon (beta): LOLA south pole 87-90S at 5 m (Barker et al. 2021), read in the browser by vrt:// from the COG USGS Astrogeology re-hosts. Lunar south polar stereographic metres relabelled as Web Mercator metres (?a_srs=EPSG:3857): the pole sits at 0,0, lunar 0E is up, scale is true at exaggeration 1. Not the Earth: no basemap, place names or geocoder apply. See /docs/beta/moon-lola.

customTerrainSources.name: MOON - LOLA south pole 87-90S 5 m (Barker 2021, PGDA 81) - VRT, metric fake-geo
customTerrainSources.description: LOLA 5 m south pole mosaic (NASA PGDA product 81, Barker et al. 2021), Float32 COG with 8 overviews on USGS's asc-pds-services bucket (CORS *, Range). public/moon/ldem_87s_5mpp.vrt names it; the URL's ?a_srs=EPSG:3857 relabels the stereographic metres as Web Mercator metres. Heights in metres above the 1737.4 km sphere.

moon-apollo15.name: Moon - Kaguya TC DTMs, Apollo 15 Hadley (beta)
moon-apollo15.description: Moon (beta): 72 Kaguya Terrain Camera stereo DTMs (USGS 2024-2026, about 15 m) around Hadley Rille, one VRT built from the USGS STAC API by docs/scripts/build-kaguya-vrt.mjs and read in the browser by vrt://. Lunar longitude and latitude are used as if they were the Earth's (true position), so the OPM Moon basemap lines up; the Moon is 3.67 times smaller than the Earth, hence exaggeration 3.67 for true proportions. See /docs/beta/moon-lola.

customTerrainSources.name: MOON - Kaguya TC DTMs v2, Apollo 15 / Hadley Rille (USGS) - VRT
customTerrainSources.description: 72 Kaguya TC stereo DTM strips (CC0, USGS Astrogeology, astrogeo-ard bucket, CORS *) in one VRT, lunar equirectangular with its seam on the farside. Built by docs/scripts/build-kaguya-vrt.mjs, hosted on the dataset-indexes release and served at /vrt/. Lunar lon/lat drawn as Earth lon/lat.

customBasemapSources.name: MOON - OpenPlanetaryMap Moon basemap (CARTO)
customBasemapSources.description: OpenPlanetaryMap's Moon basemap, Web Mercator tiles with lunar lon/lat as Earth lon/lat, CORS *.

moon-global.name: Moon - Cesium Moon Terrain, global (beta, needs a Cesium ion token)
moon-global.description: Moon (beta): the whole Moon as terrain from Cesium Moon Terrain (ion asset 2684829, LOLA and Kaguya based quantized mesh), rasterised in the browser by quantized-mesh://. Needs a Cesium ion token in Settings. True position (lunar lon/lat as Earth lon/lat, exaggeration 3.67 for true proportions) under the OPM Moon basemap. Unverified: see /docs/beta/moon-lola.

customTerrainSources.name: MOON - Cesium Moon Terrain (ion 2684829) - quantized mesh
customTerrainSources.description: Cesium Moon Terrain, a quantized-mesh tileset on Cesium ion. Every ion asset answers 401 without a token.

customBasemapSources.name: MOON - OpenPlanetaryMap Moon basemap (CARTO)
customBasemapSources.description: OpenPlanetaryMap's Moon basemap, Web Mercator tiles with lunar lon/lat as Earth lon/lat, CORS *.
